answer: A scripted farm therefore has to pad 92 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is recorded against the bridge challenge, the kernel audit can replay the opal history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A farm of 2639 identities would post 985 proofs and burn roughly 3 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
